items.title: Albert Burbank Interview, 1959-03-18
items.q: Well, the first job I played with a band. I, Zeldon Morgan, was playing over at the Artesian Hall one night

ctx.x: Do you remember any of your other early jobs then, the very first ones after that?

Well, the first job I played with a band. I, Zeldon Morgan, was playing over at the Artesian Hall one night and the client up there, Adolfo was playing over at the Artesian Hall one night and the first one night was playing with him. For some reason he couldn't so he asked me to go over there. He sent me over there. That was my first job with a band. And well I, I was pretty fair there. Just playing by ear, you know.
Did the Morgan band, the Sam and Isaiah both, did they use music ever much or did they mostly just ear players?

items.title: Albert Burbank Interview, 1962-01-04
items.q: That wasn't, uh, I was wrong, that was Ormer Bernard.

ctx.x: I think that's a good one. There's another number. I know there's a special kind of featured Kranath part. That's St. Louis Blues. I know you and Piku, Rie Lee Barnes, George Lewis, all play that one special little part, you know, that chorus. That you mean that solo? Yeah.

Well, that's a, that solo, that's been, that was on orchestration. That's the first, that's the first solo I learned to play in St. Louis Blues. Of course, I makes it a little different from because it was, you know, I could brush it up a little, but most of it is just, it was, that was written. It was written. Do you remember the first time you saw it? It was an orchestration, and all of, all of the time they played, they made that. That's when you go real high. Yeah. Well, you read it off the orchestration…
Well, he didn't play but the melody. You weren't making many variations then? No. But when did you start to do that? Well, I guess we practiced.
